t015: OPEN SOURCE · ANDROID FIRST · ALPHA PREPARATION
t019: Halo is an open-source Android assistant and cognitive runtime. It can answer with an on-device model, use real phone tools, work with your notes and study material, and extend the same runtime to connected devices. No Halo account or mandatory cloud is required.

t039: Glasses, headsets and robots extend input, output and actions instead of becoming a separate assistant.
t041: One assistant. A few clear places to work.
t042: Halo brings everyday assistance, documents, learning and connected devices into one place. Home is the assistant. Notebook is the workspace. Study turns workspace material into guided learning. t077: It can do things, not just talk about them.
t078: Halo's current Android source contains host tools for everyday phone work. The model does not receive the entire tool registry at once: Halo discovers and exposes the small set of tools relevant to the current request.

t084: External handoffs are reported as dispatched—not falsely claimed as completed.
t086: Inspect device, battery and network state; read clipboard text; fetch a web page; search files and Notebook.
t087: Sensitive reads use the tool policy and approval system rather than bypassing it.
t089: Read the current Android screen, find UI elements, and use accessibility-backed click, scroll and text entry when needed.
t090: Screen-changing accessibility actions are explicitly confirmation-gated.
t092: Requested is not the same as completed.
t093: Halo journals tool calls and outcomes before continuing the conversation. It distinguishes a successful action from a rejection, failure, external handoff or unknown completion state, and recovery is designed not to replay a completed side effect just because the app restarted.
t095: Local first. Remote when you choose it.
t096: Halo separates the runtime from the model. Changing provider changes where reasoning happens; it does not replace the assistant, workspace, tools or device layer.
t098: Halo's first-run target is Qwen 3 0.6B Dynamic INT4. After the model is installed, normal local inference does not require a Halo account or cloud service.
t101: Use Ollama, OpenCode Companion or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint on a machine you control.

t110: Free access, model availability and limits depend on the provider and may change.
t112: A selected provider failure is not permission to silently move private context to another provider.
t114: Credential storage is migrated to Android Keystore-backed secret storage instead of ordinary app preferences.
t116: Your AI should have a workspace, not a mysterious memory bucket.
t117: Halo keeps user-visible work in Notebook. You decide what enters the working context, and Study can turn a chosen source into a persistent learning session instead of hiding everything inside a chat history.
t123: Add or remove workspace objects from Halo's context deliberately instead of guessing what the assistant remembers.
t126: Keep notes, files, conversations and collections together. Canvas adds a visual space for arranging ideas, images and documents, with PDF tools being actively developed.
t128: Study sessions bind to a source revision, persist attempts before AI feedback, track review history and can narrate through Halo's speech route.
t131: Notebook storage and cognitive memory are separate concepts. Promoting something into memory is a distinct action, not an automatic side effect of writing a note.
t133: The phone is the host. Devices extend it.
t134: Halo models hardware by capability: microphone, speaker, camera, controls, sensors or physical actions. That lets the same runtime work with different devices without turning one glasses brand into the architecture.
t138: Runs the UI, runtime, local inference, system tools and workspace. Halo remains useful with no wearable connected.
t141: BLE/device control, microphone capture, media transfer and glasses-aware routing are integrated. Microphone capture has physical evidence; the latest speaker-output route still needs post-fix hardware acceptance.
t144: Android audio devices can participate as input/output endpoints. Interaction-origin routing prefers the surface where the interaction started when the route is available.
t146: A physical Halo host for proving capability, safety and action contracts. It is an experimental embodiment—not the definition of Halo.
t148: Models come and go. Your assistant shouldn't have to.
t149: Halo keeps the durable parts—context, provider choice, tools, approvals, execution truth, devices and recovery—outside any single model. Android is the first host, not the permanent boundary.
t162: Tools request semantic capabilities; hosts and devices publish what they can actually provide.
t164: Privacy policy is part of routing.
t165: Local-only and explicit provider choices are enforced before context is acquired and sent.
t167: Restarts should not duplicate side effects.
t168: The durable execution journal records claims and outcomes so recovery can continue without blindly repeating completed work.
t170: Real project. Active development. No fake “production ready” badge.
t171: Halo is preparing for early testers. Features are still changing, and the source is ahead of full physical acceptance. This page describes what exists in current source and calls out the most important validation boundaries.

t182: Read the code. Follow the evidence.
t183: Halo is open source and intentionally local-first. The repository keeps a current-state ledger so “present in code,” “tested,” and “physically accepted” do not get collapsed into one claim.
t188: You don't need smart glasses, technical experience, or your own documents. Start with a published Android build if one is available, download the free example files below, and tell us where Halo feels clear—or confusing. The test route is a guide, not an exam.

t251: Say “Give me one hint, not the answer.” Try an answer, request another explanation, then draft practice cards. They should not enter the review queue without your choice.
t254: Import or paste the sample note. Edit it, locate it again, and try sending content into Canvas if available. Check Activity for an accurate record of actions.
t257: Try voice in your language, reconnect a supported device, switch an app language, or recover from an unavailable model. Skip anything requiring hardware or credentials you don't have.
t258: A missed feature, unsupported file, failed provider, or missing permission is valuable test evidence. Record the actual outcome instead of marking a guess as success.
t260: Even a confusing button is worth reporting.
t261: Tell us which screen you were on, what you tried, what you expected and what actually happened. Include your Android and Halo versions if relevant. Never post API keys, personal files, identifiers, or unredacted private logs.
